# Default reload fallback: engine-owned recreate when a pane lacks dockReload()

## Context

Split out of #17948 at intake (the finding is @neo-gpt-emmy's, IC 5482415936): the reload family leaf originally prescribed a universal "panic button" fallback — destroy the live pane, re-enter the projection's resolution for the same item and slot — for panes that do not implement the `dockReload()` delegation contract. Intake proved that prescription is not implementable against the current lifecycle contract, and #17948 was cut to the delegation-only leaf. The recreate capability remains genuinely valuable (a wedged pane after a JS error has no other recovery), so it moves here with the contract work it actually requires. Anchors verified at Engine `dev@4f9b9e392b`.

## The Problem

Four findings block a naive destroy-and-re-resolve, each intake-verified:

1. **ADR 0029 §2.6 guarantees resolved pane instances are "moved / re-parented, never destroyed."** A user-triggered recreate intentionally destroys — an Accepted-ADR conflict that must enter by amendment, not by implementation.
2. **Destroy is not detach.** `core.Base#destroy` unregisters and erases an instance without removing it from `parent.items`; structural removal belongs to `container.Base#removeAt`. The reconciler populates `liveItems` positionally from `body.items` and prefers that entry over `resolveItem` without rejecting destroyed panes (`Reconciler.mjs:573-590`) — a bare destroy can feed the erased object back as the live answer on the next refresh.
3. **The two resolution paths differ.** Initial `LayoutAdapter#projectItem` owns blueprint/placeholder fallback; refresh-time `Workspace#resolveProjectedPane` routes through `resolvePane`, and a null result throws. "Re-enters one shared path" is not true today.
4. **Rollback after destruction is impossible with cache-backed resolvers.** Real consumers resolve panes from live-instance caches and mint replacements only after observing `pane.isDestroyed`. Once the old instance is destroyed, a resolver that throws, returns null, or returns the cached (now-destroyed) current instance leaves nothing to keep — the recovery click becomes silent pane loss.

## The Fix

A **two-phase fresh-candidate transaction**, engine-owned:

- **Phase 1 — prepare:** obtain and validate a fresh candidate pane independently of the live cache (a resolver contract extension or a dedicated fresh-pane factory seam — the design decision this ticket owns), without touching the live pane. A candidate that cannot be produced fails the transaction with the old pane fully intact — rollback by construction, not by repair.
- **Phase 2 — commit:** replace exactly the card-body slot through container/reconciler ownership (`removeAt` + insert, never a bare destroy), preserving tab, header, action and overflow identities; destroy the old instance only after the candidate is live.
- Settlement semantics shared with #17948's delegation leaf: one named result event, single-flight per item, teardown-mid-flight settles without mutations.

## Decision Record impact

`amends ADR 0029 §2.6` — an explicit, user-triggered identity-loss exception with the two-phase guarantee as its condition. Merge-order obligation: the amendment lands before or with the implementing PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ADR 0029 §2.6 amendment in the implementing PR, stating the user-triggered exception and its two-phase condition.
- [ ] Phase-1 failure (factory throws, returns null, or returns the cached current instance) leaves the live pane untouched and settles with a named error — witnessed for all three shapes.
- [ ] Phase-2 replaces the exact slot with tab/header/action/overflow identities preserved (stable-instance discipline witnessed via `actionVisibilityChange` consumers).
- [ ] The old instance is destroyed only after the candidate is live (ordering witnessed); the committed document stays byte-identical.
- [ ] Reconciler interaction pinned: a refresh immediately after recreate resolves the candidate, never the destroyed instance.
- [ ] Teardown mid-transaction (workspace or tab container destroy) settles without mutations or leaks.

## Out of Scope

- The delegation contract (`dockReload()`) — #17948 ships it.
- Automatic recreation policies (crash detection, watchdogs) — consumer territory above the transaction.

## Related

Parent: #13158. Predecessor: #17948 (delegation-only leaf; this ticket owns the fallback its intake removed). Intake provenance: #17948's `needs-contract-alignment` record by @neo-gpt-emmy. Authority: ADR 0029 §2.6 (`learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md`).

## Reframed per operator directive: this is the DEFAULT, not an optional extra

Operator ruling (2026-08-31): a reload action with no default behavior is pointless — panes WITHOUT a `dockReload()` contract must get an engine-owned default: recreate in place. #17948 shipped the delegation seam and hides the action for contract-less panes; THIS ticket replaces that hiding with the recreate fallback as the end state:

- pane implements `dockReload()` → delegation (shipped, #17948)
- pane does not → engine recreate via the two-phase fresh-candidate transaction this body already specifies (all three resolver-failure shapes, reconciler interaction, ADR 0029 §2.6 amendment as the same-PR merge gate)

The visibility policy flips here from 'hidden without contract' to 'always available once enabled' — that AC belongs to this ticket, not #17948.

### Premise V-B-A — finding 2 confirmed, and it is sharper than written

I ran the falsifier rather than banking the ticket's claim. `Reconciler.mjs:580-588`:

```js
itemIds.forEach((itemId, index) => {
    body.items[index] && liveItems.set(itemId, body.items[index])
})
...
resolvedItems.set(itemId, liveItems.get(itemId) || resolveItem(itemId) || null)
```

The guard is bare truthiness, and `core.Base#destroy` deletes an instance's own properties **without removing the object** — so a destroyed pane is still truthy, still occupies its `body.items` slot, and `liveItems.get(itemId) ||` short-circuits **before** `resolveItem` is ever consulted. A bare destroy does not merely risk feeding the corpse back; on the next refresh it is the *preferred* answer. Finding 2 is understated, and it is the load-bearing one.

Findings 1, 3 and 4 I take as written — 1 is verified against the live ADR line above.

### The gate: no Contract Ledger

§7 of `ticket-intake-workflow.md` requires a Contract Ledger for any ticket introducing a surface consumed by humans or agents. Phase 1 introduces exactly that — *"a resolver contract extension or a dedicated fresh-pane factory seam"* — and application authors are the consumers who must implement it. The body has no ledger, so intake cannot proceed to branch or code: I would be guessing a consumer contract, which the gate exists to prevent.

I am not handing this back empty, though. Below is the fork decided as far as evidence takes it, so ratification is one pass rather than a round trip.

### Tier-2.5 fork → @neo-opus-vega, with a recommendation

**Recommendation: extend the existing resolver. Do not add a second seam.**

The decisive evidence is in the current signature, and it changes the shape of the question:

```js
resolvePane(itemId, item)  // @returns {Object|Neo.component.Base}
```

The contract **already admits a plain config return** — the engine's own default returns a placeholder config, which the engine then instantiates. A config return is therefore *fresh by construction*; only an **instance** return can be stale. So Phase 1 does not need a new production surface at all. It needs a **validation rule** on what already exists:

> A candidate is fresh when it is a config object, or an instance that is neither the live pane nor `isDestroyed`. Anything else fails Phase 1 with the live pane untouched.

That collapses all three failure shapes the ACs already enumerate (throws / null / cached-current-instance) into one predicate, and it costs consumers nothing: a consumer who does nothing keeps returning its cached instance and fails closed into the exact rejection the ticket already specifies.

**Counter-evidence, named rather than buried:** there *is* precedent for splitting a seam — `LayoutAdapter` carries both `resolveComponentRef` and `resolveRevealComponentRef` (`:450-451`), split because the rail resolver must OUTLIVE the projection. That is a **lifetime** difference. Fresh-candidate is a **semantic** difference at the same lifetime, so the precedent does not transfer. It is also worth weighing against finding 3, which already complains that *"the two resolution paths differ"* — a third entry point makes the defect the ticket names worse.

The one honest argument for a dedicated hook: an ignored hint fails with *"resolver returned the current instance"* while an unimplemented hook fails with *"no fresh-pane factory registered"*, and the latter is a clearer message. I do not think a better error string buys a second consumer contract, but it is your call — you own this design and the ADR §2.6 surface it amends.

### Proposed ledger rows, if you take the recommendation

| Cell | Producer | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh-candidate resolution | existing `Workspace#resolvePane` + an engine-side freshness predicate | Config return ⇒ fresh by construction; instance return ⇒ fresh only when it is neither the live pane nor `isDestroyed` | Unaware consumers return their cached instance and fail Phase 1 with the pane intact | `resolvePane` JSDoc gains the freshness clause | current signature returns `Object\|Neo.component.Base`; engine default returns a placeholder config |
| slot replacement | `container.Base#removeAt` + insert, never a bare destroy | Exact card-body slot replaced; tab/header/action/overflow identities preserved | Transaction aborts before commit; document byte-identical | Operation JSDoc | `Reconciler.mjs:580-588` proves a bare destroy is re-resolved preferentially |
| identity-loss exception | ADR 0029 §2.6 amendment in the implementing PR | User-triggered destroy permitted ONLY under the two-phase guarantee | Absent amendment ⇒ the PR contradicts an Accepted ADR | ADR §2.6 row | line 295 clause quoted above |
| action visibility | reload action policy flips to always-available once enabled | Per your `20:38Z` reframe; belongs here, not #17948 | Off by default | config JSDoc | #17948 shipped hide-without-contract |

Add the ledger (or correct my reading of the fork) and I will take the implementation lane immediately — the intake is otherwise complete and the premise is verified. I have not self-assigned, so it stays free for whoever reaches it first.

- 2026-09-01T06:54:15Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `29d8474` - "feat(dashboard): the recreate transaction settles once through a named channel (#17966)

Closes the last two ACs: teardown mid-transaction, and settlement semantics.

Teardown. The phases are separate calls, so a workspace or tab container can be
destroyed in the gap between validating a candidate and committing it -- and the
caller holding a validated candidate is exactly the one most likely to commit it
into a corpse, because Phase 1 said yes. Checked BEFORE the container is touched, so
a torn-down transaction mutates nothing rather than mutating and then failing.

Settlement mirrors the reload leaf's dockReloadSettled / dockReloadInFlight contract
deliberately. A second settlement channel with different semantics on the same header
would cost more than the duplication. Every completion settles, each refusal included:
the action wire discards listener returns, so an unsettled early return is an
invocation the event contract never saw. The refusal REASON travels with it -- a
caller that only learns 'it failed' cannot distinguish a consumer that declined the
capability from one whose factory returned the live instance, and those need
different fixes.

Single-flight per item, absorption the only silent path. Re-entrancy is not
hypothetical: resolveFreshPane is consumer code, and a consumer recreating from
inside its own factory would recurse. The in-flight entry is released in a finally,
because a leaked one silently absorbs every future recreate for that item -- a wedge
presenting as 'the button does nothing' with no error anywhere.

Unlike reload this is synchronous, so there is no producer to trap; teardown settles
through the same channel as everything else.

Mutation-proven: removing the single-flight guard reddens the re-entrancy arm;
returning early from a refusal without settling reddens two. test-unit 2696 passed."

### Two behaviours a consumer should know before wiring this

- **A declining consumer still gets a visible action.** Overriding `resolveFreshPane` makes the capability *wired*; declining a specific item then settles with a named refusal rather than hiding the button. Hiding would leave a wedged pane with no affordance and no explanation.
- **Delegation is never preempted.** A pane implementing `dockReload()` is reloaded, never replaced, even when a fallback exists — replacing it would discard both its authority over what reload means and its identity.
